description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of various parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods across different model sizes, with the x-axis representing the model size categories—ranging from "Small" to "Large"—and the y-axis indicating the performance metric, which is the average accuracy in percentage. Each bar corresponds to a specific fine-tuning method, including "LoRA," "Adapter," "Prefix Tuning," "BitFit," and "Full Fine-Tuning," with distinct colors for each method. The chart shows that "Full Fine-Tuning" consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all model sizes, followed by "LoRA" and "Adapter," while "Prefix Tuning" and "BitFit" exhibit lower performance. The performance of all methods generally increases with model size, but the gap between "Full Fine-Tuning" and the others widens as the model size grows, indicating that larger models benefit more from full fine-tuning. The bars are arranged in ascending order of model size from left to right, and the performance values are clearly labeled on top of each bar, allowing for easy comparison. The chart also includes a legend in the top right corner that identifies each method by color, and the title "Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces" is displayed at the top, providing context for the data presented.
